title: One Chain, Two Answers, Set by Time

scenes.tts: Give a P C twelve cell the growth factor E G F, and it divides. Give the same cell N G F, and it stops dividing and grows long, nerve-like fibres. Both signals run through the same four proteins: Ras, Raf, Mek and Erk. How can one chain of enzymes carry two instructions?
scenes.caption: Give a PC12 cell the growth factor EGF, and it divides. Give the same cell NGF, and it stops dividing and grows long, nerve-like fibres. Both signals run through the same four proteins: Ras, Raf, MEK and ERK. How can one chain of enzymes carry two instructions?
scenes.visual: A box marked with a question mark stands for the cell. EGF enters it and a cell divides; NGF enters it and a cell grows fibres. The box then fills with the four proteins, Ras, Raf, MEK and ERK, and both answers are marked with question marks.
scenes.narration: Give a PC12 cell the growth factor EGF, and it divides. Give the same cell NGF, and it stops dividing and grows long, nerve-like fibres. Both signals run through the same four proteins: Ras, Raf, MEK and ERK. How can one chain of enzymes carry two instructions?

scenes.tts: At the membrane, S O S loads Ras with G T P, and Ras is on. Ras is not a kinase, so it works by contact. Active Ras catches Raf, a kinase that floats in the cytosol, folded shut. Binding brings Raf to the membrane and helps pull it open. Then two Raf molecules pair, side by side, and pairing is needed for normal activation.
scenes.caption: At the membrane, SOS loads Ras with GTP, and Ras is on. Ras is not a kinase, so it works by contact. Active Ras catches Raf, a kinase that floats in the cytosol, folded shut. Binding brings Raf to the membrane and helps pull it open. Then two Raf molecules pair, side by side, and pairing is needed for normal activation.
scenes.visual: Zoomed on the membrane: Ras is a mouth on the membrane. SOS swaps its GDP tag for GTP and the mouth opens. A folded Raf drifts in, the mouth takes hold of its front half and the fold swings open; a second Raf joins beside it and the pair turns green.
scenes.narration: At the membrane, SOS loads Ras with GTP, and Ras is on. Ras is not a kinase, so it works by contact. Active Ras catches Raf, a kinase that floats in the cytosol, folded shut. Binding brings Raf to the membrane and helps pull it open. Then two Raf molecules pair, side by side, and pairing is needed for normal activation.

scenes.tts: Active Raf adds phosphates to the next kinase, Mek, on two serines. Mek then does something unusual. It adds a phosphate to a threonine and another to a tyrosine, one residue apart, on Erk. Erk needs both. Take either one off, and Erk goes quiet.
scenes.caption: Active Raf adds phosphates to the next kinase, MEK, on two serines. MEK then does something unusual. It adds a phosphate to a threonine and another to a tyrosine, one residue apart, on ERK. ERK needs both. Take either one off, and ERK goes quiet.
scenes.visual: The view pulls back to a staircase: the Raf pair, then MEK, then ERK. Two phosphates hop from Raf to two serine sites on MEK; MEK turns green and passes one phosphate each to the neighbouring threonine and tyrosine sites on ERK. Take one off and ERK goes grey.
scenes.narration: Active Raf adds phosphates to the next kinase, MEK, on two serines. MEK then does something unusual. It adds a phosphate to a threonine and another to a tyrosine, one residue apart, on ERK. ERK needs both. Take either one off, and ERK goes quiet.

scenes.tts: Negative feedback sets how long the signal lasts, and Erk supplies its own. Active Erk phosphorylates proteins above it in the chain, among them S O S and Raf, and that weakens them. It also turns on genes for phosphatases, enzymes that take both phosphates back off Erk. That second kind of feedback is slower, because a protein has to be made.
scenes.caption: Negative feedback sets how long the signal lasts, and ERK supplies its own. Active ERK phosphorylates proteins above it in the chain, among them SOS and Raf, and that weakens them. It also turns on genes for phosphatases, enzymes that take both phosphates back off ERK. That second kind of feedback is slower, because a protein has to be made.
scenes.visual: The whole active chain with a clock. Red arrows run from ERK back up to Raf and to SOS and dim them. ERK turns on a gene; a dashed phosphatase waits beside it, the clock sweeps, the phosphatase becomes solid and strips both phosphates off ERK.
scenes.narration: Negative feedback sets how long the signal lasts, and ERK supplies its own. Active ERK phosphorylates proteins above it in the chain, among them SOS and Raf, and that weakens them. It also turns on genes for phosphatases, enzymes that take both phosphates back off ERK. That second kind of feedback is slower, because a protein has to be made.

scenes.tts: Different stimuli leave the pathway on for different lengths of time before feedback closes the window. In a P C twelve cell, Erk activity after E G F rises and falls back within about an hour. After N G F, it climbs to a plateau that lasts for hours. In nineteen ninety-five, Christopher Marshall proposed that this difference is itself the instruction. A brief signal goes with division, and a sustained one with differentiation.
scenes.caption: Different stimuli leave the pathway on for different lengths of time before feedback closes the window. In a PC12 cell, ERK activity after EGF rises and falls back within about an hour. After NGF, it climbs to a plateau that lasts for hours. In 1995, Christopher Marshall proposed that this difference is itself the instruction. A brief signal goes with division, and a sustained one with differentiation.
scenes.visual: Two rows share a time axis. Green windows of different lengths open and a red edge closes each. ERK activity after EGF rises and falls back within about an hour; after NGF it climbs to a plateau that runs on. The difference in length is marked as the instruction, and the short row ends in a dividing cell, the long row in fibres.
scenes.narration: Different stimuli leave the pathway on for different lengths of time before feedback closes the window. In a PC12 cell, ERK activity after EGF rises and falls back within about an hour. After NGF, it climbs to a plateau that lasts for hours. In 1995, Christopher Marshall proposed that this difference is itself the instruction. A brief signal goes with division, and a sustained one with differentiation.

scenes.tts: Now force Mek on for good, with no growth factor at all. Erk then stays on without end, which the cell cannot tell apart from a long N G F signal. In nineteen ninety-four, Cowley and Marshall did this, and P C twelve cells grew fibres with no N G F. One caution: this rule comes from one cell line, and how widely it holds is an open question. So keep this rule: in a P C twelve cell, how long Erk stays on carries the instruction.
scenes.caption: Now force MEK on for good, with no growth factor at all. ERK then stays on without end, which the cell cannot tell apart from a long NGF signal. In 1994, Cowley and Marshall did this, and PC12 cells grew fibres with no NGF. One caution: this rule comes from one cell line, and how widely it holds is an open question. So keep this rule: in a PC12 cell, how long ERK stays on carries the instruction.
scenes.visual: NGF is struck out. An always-on MEK holds ERK on without end, a plateau that matches the NGF curve, and the PC12 cell grows fibres. A row of other cells with question marks shows that how widely this holds is open; the plateau is then marked: how long ERK stays on.
scenes.narration: Now force MEK on for good, with no growth factor at all. ERK then stays on without end, which the cell cannot tell apart from a long NGF signal.
